disclaimer: Editorially source-checked statements are not independently formally verified theorem databases; always inspect original source and exact premises.

items.title: Rosenthal potential and pure equilibrium
items.statement: Every finite unweighted congestion game in the Rosenthal model has an exact potential and at least one pure Nash equilibrium.
assumptions: Each strategy is a subset of resources
Resource delay is a function of the number of users
items.scope_note: Does not apply to all weighted congestion games; does not bound Price of Anarchy.

items.title: Pure equilibria may fail in weighted congestion
items.statement: There are weighted congestion games, including weighted network games, that do not admit a pure Nash equilibrium.
items.scope_note: Existence can be recovered under special assumptions, including some linear delay settings; this is a counterexample to universal existence.

items.title: PoA for finite unweighted linear-latency congestion games
items.statement: For finite congestion games with nonnegative linear latency functions and social cost defined as the sum of players' costs, the tight pure price of anarchy bound is 5/2.
assumptions: Sum of player costs as objective
items.scope_note: Not a claim for arbitrary latency functions, weighted games, or all definitions of social cost.

items.title: Illustrative Bayesian equilibrium in first-price auction
items.statement: For n risk-neutral bidders with i.i.d. values uniform on [0,1] in a standard single-item first-price auction, bidding (n−1)/n times private value is a symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium.
items.scope_note: An illustrative equilibrium formula, not a universal PoA guarantee.

items.title: Truthful bidding is weakly dominant in standard second-price auction
items.statement: In a standard single-item second-price auction with private values and quasilinear payoff, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy.
items.scope_note: Does not claim truthful equilibria are the only Nash equilibria.

items.title: EFX is distinct from EFX0
items.statement: In the standard indivisible-goods setting, EFX checks removal of any positively valued item, while a stronger EFX0 variant also checks items of zero value.
items.scope_note: Definitions may differ when chores, mixed items, or externalities are allowed.

items.title: Distributional prediction for ski rental with unknown error
items.statement: For ski rental with buy cost b, the cited paper gives an expected-cost upper bound of OPT + O(min(max(eta,1)*sqrt(b), b*log(b))), with eta the Wasserstein-1 distance between the predicted and true distributions; the algorithm does not require eta as input.
assumptions: Classical ski rental with buy cost b
Unknown true distribution over ski days
items.scope_note: From the paper abstract; constants, edge cases and lower-bound conditions must be checked in the source. Not a universal result for arbitrary online problems.

items.title: Binary search with distributional advice
items.statement: The cited paper gives query complexity O(H(p) + log(eta)) under its distributional prediction and error conventions, with H(p) the target distribution entropy and eta the Earth Mover's Distance to the prediction.
assumptions: Known or unknown true target distribution per paper model
items.scope_note: Asymptotic expression is taken from the abstract and depends on the paper's conventions when eta is small; consult the paper for exact logarithmic normalization.

items.title: Gibbs sampling gives approximation and sensitivity tradeoffs for matching
items.statement: The paper constructs, for every fixed approximation parameter epsilon > 0, an (1-epsilon)-approximation matching algorithm with sensitivity Delta^{O(1/epsilon)} for bounded-degree graphs, using Gibbs-distribution sampling.
assumptions: Specified edge-deletion perturbation and Wasserstein/Hamming output metric
epsilon positive and relevant runtime constraints
items.scope_note: From the abstract. The result does not apply without qualification to weighted matchings, all output metrics, or DP noise calibration.

items.title: Metric voting combines sensitivity, privacy and sub-three distortion
items.statement: The cited paper studies randomized metric voting rules with distortion strictly below three and separate stability/privacy guarantees under one-voter deletion or replacement, respectively.
assumptions: One-voter replacement for approximate differential privacy
items.scope_note: The sensitivity and privacy guarantees use different adjacency conventions, and the paper's constants and distributions must be consulted for formal statements.

items.title: Private cut optimization via shifting and other mechanisms
items.statement: The cited paper gives edge-differentially private approximation algorithms for multiway cut and minimum k-cut; for constant k it reports optimal additive-error scaling O(k log n) when privacy parameters are fixed.
assumptions: Privacy parameter treated as fixed for the quoted asymptotic
items.scope_note: Shifting mechanism addresses part of the suite; minimum k-cut uses a different exponential mechanism argument. Do not attribute every bound to shifting.
